start.advice:
This game lives from its mood.
It is at its best with headphones, or somewhere quiet.
notebook.title: Notebook
notebook.unknown: something I do not know yet
pause.title: Pause
pause.confirm:
Start over from the beginning?
Everything you have done so far will be lost.
old_man.before: There you are. Evening is coming.
The lanterns, as always. All three. Don't forget the one by the bridge.
And when you are back … wind the music box for me. My fingers won't do it any more.
I have to be off then. I am late.
old_man.before_again: The lanterns first. Then the music box.
music_box.later: A small music box. The crank is already in place.
table.before: A book lies on the table.
It lies there as if it always had.
stranger.before: You are early today. Or I am late. The brook is loud tonight, do you hear?
child.before: I am counting the lights. When you are done, there are three.
arch.before: The arch to the mill hill.
Not today. The old man is waiting.
music_box.evening: The crank turns heavily. Then the tune begins.
The old man listens. His lips move along.
Then he gets up and takes his coat.
old_man.leaving: That is how it went. Just so.
I have to be off. You go ahead, I will be right behind you.
rift.comes: In the doorway I hear the tune behind me. It grows slower. Deeper.
rift.wake: Grass. Wind from the wrong side.
I am lying by the path. For how long?
lantern.blown: Then the wind carries it off.
stranger.wind: You come across the bridge. Nobody has done that for a long time.
Since the Rift no wick here will catch. The wind is a different one.
As a child I always sat behind the big stone when it blew. It was still behind it. You could even … oh, that does not belong here.
It is dark in front of the old man's door. Dark means: nobody home. Then you do not knock either.
stranger.house_lit: There is light at the old man's. Then he is home.
Behind a stone, you say? Yes. It never blew behind it. I knew that as a child.
The wind is a different one all the same. It was not always like this.
stranger.evening: Do you feel that? The wind is the old one again.
I walked along the brook here every evening. As far as the bridge, always the same steps. My feet still know.
That evening … all the lanterns went out at once. Before any wind blew. I do not forget that.
stranger.whole: Now it is my evening again.
You used to pass here every evening. I never asked where to.
child.shy: You do not have it with you.
child.still: The book! You always had that with you.
I stand here every day. If you are very still, it comes back. Only here.
There was something over there. You could walk through it.
child.bright: That evening it was all bright. Like noon. Nobody believes me.
memory.bridge: The stone lay beside the bridge, in the grass. Not on the path.
arch.dark: An arch of old stones. Behind it there is only sky.
arch.skips: That was not the way back.
old_man.first: Sit down. No. You never sit down.
There is a book on the table. It has been lying there for as long as I can think. The writing is not mine.
old_man.take_it: The book. There on the table.
Take it. It has been looking at you all this time.
notebook.taken: A small notebook. The first pages are written on.
What I have learned today is already in it.
old_man.borrowed: The music box is silent. Do you hear? Exactly.
I always wound it with … it is in the cupboard. It is not mine.
I hand out nothing unless I know whose it is. I have always been like that. I think.
cupboard.guarded: What lies in there is borrowed. Tell me from whom, then we shall see.
old_man.yours: The miller, you say? The miller! Of course.
Then it is his. Take it to him. And greet him. He will know from whom.
cupboard.crank: He opens the cupboard. Between old blankets lies a heavy iron crank.
old_man.carry: The music box can wait. It has been waiting a long time.
old_man.waiting: You took it to him? Good.
It is quiet here without the music box. I am waiting.
old_man.wind_it: He gave it back to you?
old_man.humming: Hm-hm, hmm … that is how it went. Just so.
In the evenings I always went up somewhere. Every evening.
Where to … it will not come to me.
old_man.above: A great light, you say. Above the water.
The watch. I lit it every evening. Every one.
That evening I was just about to leave. I still heard the music box. It was running backwards.
I cannot get up there any more. My legs no longer know the way.
Here. The wick. It will not burn without it. You go.
old_man.go: Go on. I will listen to the music box.
When it burns up there, I shall see it from the window.
music_box.silent: A small music box. It is silent.
Where the crank should sit there is an empty hole.
music_box.wrong: The tune comes out crooked, too low, as if under water. Something outside is still wrong.
music_box.plays: The tune. As on the evening before everything tore.
The old man lifts his head.
music_box.playing: It is playing. Softly, without end.
miller.crank: Since the Rift she stands still. Not a sail moves. Not a breath of air up here.
The crank is missing. I lent it out. To someone who wanted to wind something. Something small.
To whom … it is on the tip of my tongue. Has been for weeks. Or years.
I stand here every evening and watch the weather. Now there is none.
miller.have_crank: That is it! Where from … never mind.
Put it on. Right beside the door.
mill.stuck: Where the crank should sit there is only an empty hole.
mill.turns: The crank catches. A creak, then the sails turn.
The wind is back. The right one.
mill.backwards: The crank catches. The sails turn.
But backwards. The wind comes and goes again, all at once.
mill.backwards_look: The crank sits firm. That is not the reason.
miller.backwards: The wrong way round. Like that she grinds nothing, she only takes.
She goes by the vane over there. And the vane … where did it point again?
Here, where I stand, I used to know at once. Stand beside me and keep still. Maybe you see more than I do.
vane.right: The sails stop. Then they turn the other way.
The wind is back. The right one.
vane.idle: A weather vane. It points to the edge of the hill.
Not a breath of air. It does not stir.
vane.unsure: But which way did it point?
vane.fixed: The miller has fastened the weather vane.
miller.dry: The field. Look at it. It always got its water in the morning, from above, from the spring.
There has been no morning for a long time.
miller.grain: Grain! She has grain in her again. Now she will not stop any more.
Here, the crank. She only needed it to start. Take it back to the one who … you know whom.
That evening the sails stood still for a moment. In full wind. That does not happen.
miller.whole: You used to come up here often. You never bought any flour.
memory.mill: And the weather vane points another way than now.
raft.away: A raft used to lead across the brook here.
Now it lies up in the pool, on the far bank. The wind must have driven it over.
sluice.opens: The sluice gives way. The water runs off, down the brook.
sluice.closes: The sluice shuts. The brook grows thin, then still.
Below, the bed lies dry again.
steps.flooded: Steps leading down into the bed of the brook.
Now the water rushes over them. Nobody gets down there while the sluice is open.
steps.flooded_up: The steps up to the spring.
fisher.mud: Oh. Nobody has come from up there for a long time.
I only wanted to get home. Over there, the house. Do you see it?
No boat goes in the mud. The water always came in the morning and went in the evening. It has been evening ever since.
And without the light on the island I do not go out anyway. At low water you could walk across, over the stones. But I … I would rather stay with the boat.
fisher.no_light: But the light on the island is out. Without the light I do not go. My mother once went without.
You could only reach the island on foot, over the stones. At low water. Now they lie under water.
fisher.light_on: The light! It burns again. I always steered by it.
But nobody goes in the mud. The water always came in the morning, from above.
fisher.row: Water, and the light is burning.
Get in. I am going home.
boat.hers: A rowing boat. It belongs to the fisherwoman.
boat.mud: The boat lies in the mud.
fisher.home: Home. You can take the boat whenever you like.
I sat here on the jetty every evening. From the water you could see the great light up above. Only the old man went up.
That evening it was still mirrored in the pond when it had already gone out above. I looked up and down again. Twice.
fisher.whole: You sometimes came along in the boat. You never said where you wanted to go.
memory.jetty: Above the water, high up: a great light.
There is another piece. One that nobody knows any more.
view.mill_hill.lit: The sails turn in the light.
view.pond.lit: The light on the island is burning.
big_light.dark: A great fire bowl on a pillar. Cold.
big_light.weak: The wick is in. The flame stays small and cowers.
Below, it is not bright everywhere yet. Alone it does not carry.
big_light.lit: The wick is in. The flame takes and straightens.
Below, the lights answer. The village. The mill. The spring. The pond.
And beyond it, in the dark: other pieces. Many. None of them has a light.
The Rift is not over. It is only over here.
big_light.burns: Beyond it many pieces still lie in the dark.
memory.lookout: First the great light burned. Then, one after the other, the lights below.
note.village.title: The village
note.village.text: A piece of land hanging in the void. I know its paths before I walk them.
note.mill_hill.title: The mill hill
note.mill_hill.text: A hill with a windmill. Up here it is still. The wind for the whole valley comes from here.
note.spring.title: The spring
note.spring.text: A pool from which the brook rises. A sluice holds the water back. Steps lead down into the bed of the brook.
note.pond.title: The pond
note.pond.text: A piece nobody up there spoke of any more. Since it stands in this book, the arch at the spring leads here.
note.watch.title: The watch
note.watch.text: The highest place of the valley. The great light burned here every evening. The old man lit it.
note.lee_of_stone.title: Behind the stone
note.lee_of_stone.text: As a child the woman by the brook sat behind the big stone when it blew. It was still behind it.
note.light_means_home.title: Light at the door
note.light_means_home.text: In the village a dark house means: nobody home. Then you do not knock either.
note.lent_thing.title: Something borrowed
note.lent_thing.text: In the old man's cupboard lies the thing he wound the music box with. It is not his. He no longer knows whose.
note.millers_crank.title: The miller's crank
note.millers_crank.text: The miller lent out his crank, to someone who wanted to wind something small. He no longer knows to whom.
note.still_place.title: Where it comes back
note.still_place.text: The child says: where somebody stands every day, it comes back if you are very still. Only there. I have to stand beside them and wait.
note.field_thirsty.title: The field
note.field_thirsty.text: The field on the mill hill got its water in the morning, from the spring. Without grain the mill runs empty.
note.morning_water.title: Water in the morning
note.morning_water.text: The water came in the morning and went in the evening. Somebody shut the sluice for the night. The Rift came in the evening.
note.island_light.title: The light on the island
note.island_light.text: The fisherwoman only goes out when the light on the island burns. You reach the island on foot, over stones, at low water.
note.evening_walk.title: Along the brook in the evening
note.evening_walk.text: The woman walked along the brook every evening, as far as the bridge. Always the same steps.
note.fishers_evening.title: The jetty
note.fishers_evening.text: The fisherwoman sat on the jetty by her house every evening. From there you could see a great light above the water.
note.arch_village.title: The arch in the village
note.arch_village.text: A stone arch stood at the eastern edge. When I remembered it, it stood there again.
note.stone_places.title: The stone by the bridge
note.stone_places.text: It lay beside the bridge in the grass. Not on the path and not in front of the house.
note.vane_direction.title: The weather vane
note.vane_direction.text: From the miller's place I saw the mill as it was. The vane pointed towards the mill.
note.big_light.title: The great light
note.big_light.text: From the fisherwoman's jetty I saw it: a great light high above the water. There must be another piece up there.
note.lookout.title: The old man's place
note.lookout.text: He stood on the watch every evening. First the great light burned, then the lights below, one after the other.
note.rift_stranger.title: The Rift: the lanterns
note.rift_stranger.text: The woman by the brook says: all the lanterns went out at once, before any wind blew.
note.rift_miller.title: The Rift: the sails
note.rift_miller.text: The miller says: the sails stood still for a moment, in full wind.
note.rift_child.title: The Rift: the brightness
note.rift_child.text: The child says: it was all bright, like noon. Yet it was evening.
note.rift_fisher.title: The Rift: the mirror
note.rift_fisher.text: The fisherwoman says: the great light was still mirrored in the pond when it had already gone out above.
note.rift_old_man.title: The Rift: the music box
note.rift_old_man.text: The old man says: he was just about to leave and heard the music box. It was running backwards. I was there. I only heard it grow slower.
